title: Enhanced biodiesel synthesis from sunflower oil in an integrated plasma‐jet and bubble reactor
content:
Abstract

Biodiesel is a renewable alternative to fossil fuels, and sunflower oil is a promising feedstock because of its favorable fatty-acid composition. This study developed and optimized an integrated atmospheric plasma jet-bubble reactor for the transesterification of refined sunflower oil. The configuration combines plasma exposure at the liquid surface with gas-induced mixing from the bottom of the reactor while mechanical stirring is maintained. A four-factor Box–Behnken design was used to evaluate temperature, methanol-to-oil molar ratio, KOH concentration, and residence time. The model predicted optimum conditions of 42.51°C, a methanol-to-oil molar ratio of 5.79:1, 0.97 wt% KOH, and a residence time of 29.92 min, corresponding to a predicted FAME content of 95.89%. A confirmation experiment yielded 94.36% FAME. These findings demonstrate the potential of the integrated plasma jet–bubble reactor as a process-intensification strategy for achieving high FAME content within a relatively short residence time. Further investigation of energy consumption, fuel properties, and plasma-assisted reaction mechanisms is required to establish its broader practical and sustainability benefits.
